title: Cross-team priority handoff + tactical decisions — 2027-09-14
content:
Meeting: Cross-team engineering leadership weekly
Date: 2027-09-14 10:00–11:00 PT
Location: Zoom / #eng-leads
Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Note-taker: Marco Ruiz
Attendees: Aisha Patel, Marco Ruiz, Sofia Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Menon, Evan Brooks, Jenna Park (guest), Rahul Das (observability)

Agenda:
1) Quick signals (3m each team)
2) Triage: hot cache-eviction regression and customer impact
3) Capacity & Dedicated pool bump decision
4) Rollout windows and risky changes next 2 weeks
5) Cross-team blockers / handoffs / action items
6) AOB (timeboxed)

Quick signals (high level)
- Serving-runtime: 95th latency rose by ~12% for mid-size prompt mix since 2027-09-11; root cause suspected related to new LRU/KV-change in PR #1209. (Sofia)
- Observability: anomaly detected across EU region for cache hit metric; snapshots saved, traced back to same time window as latency spike. (Rahul)
- Platform-engineering: autoshare autoscaler behaved correctly but queueing increased; no infra provisioning failures. (Liam)
- Private deployments: one on-prem customer reported degraded throughput with long-running KV sessions; reproduced on staging. (Priya)
- Solutions/SE: field reports of 3 customers with higher tail latency and a couple putting support tickets as P2. (Jenna)

Spotlight: cache-eviction regression (high priority)
- Timeline: change merged 2027-09-10 (PR #1209), latency increase observed 2027-09-11, alerting escalated 2027-09-12.
- Hypothesis: new LRU heuristic triggers more frequent prefix eviction under multi-tenant load patterns, increasing KV warmup requests and recomputation.
- Evidence: flamegraphs and KV metrics show increased cache miss rate on sequences with heavy reuse; repro on staging using customer request traces reproduces 10–15% latency degradation.
- Impact: host-level tail latency increase, several dedicated customers on shared pools reported client-visible spikes. No data loss, but SLO alerts fired for 2 customers.

Decision: immediate rollback vs. guarded disable
- Decision reached (consensus): revert the LRU heuristic change in hosted and dedicated shared pools for now, while keeping the change enabled in a private test pool for further instrumentation.
- Rationale: revert minimizes customer impact quickly; retains an isolated testbed to collect traces and refine heuristic.
- Owner: Sofia Chen to coordinate rollback and patch.
- Target: rollback deployed by 2027-09-15 03:00 PT in hosted and shared dedicated pools (low-traffic window).

Capacity discussion: short-term bump for Dedicated pools
- Problem: during the latency spike, some customers experienced degraded effective throughput. Dedicated capacity for a few tenants sits near committed utilization with little burst headroom.
- Proposal: temporarily increase burst-capacity floor for affected dedicated pools by +15% for 72 hours while we stabilize the rollback and monitor.
- Cost: estimated incremental spend ~$14k USD for 72 hours across affected pools. Finance has pre-approved one-off operational spend for incident mitigation up to $25k.
- Decision: approve temporary bump.
- Owner: Liam O'Connor to schedule capacity increase with infra and finance; complete by 2027-09-15 05:00 PT.

Rollout windows & risky changes (next 2 weeks)
- Freeze for serving-runtime heuristics: no LRU/KV heuristic code merges until 2027-09-22 without explicit sign-off from eng-leads.
- Allowed: low-risk optimizations (observability-only, logging tweaks) if feature-flagged.
- Gate: any change touching caching, batching, or routing requires a short canary in private test pool + perf traces for at least 24 hrs.

Cross-team blockers / handoffs
- Observability: need additional tracing instrumentation inside KV cache path to capture eviction decisions and owning request id. Blocker: shortage of tracing quota for production. (Rahul)
  - Action: Priya to coordinate temporary allocation of tracing quota and update instrumentation plan. Due 2027-09-16.
- Private Deployments: replication of the regression on on-prem suggests config mismatch for KV persistence. Need a mapping of config differences. (Priya)
  - Action: Priya + Evan to produce config-diff doc and recommended patch for customers. Due 2027-09-17.
- SE / CS: need a concise customer-facing incident summary and recommended mitigation steps to share with affected accounts. (Jenna)
  - Action: Marco to draft incident go-to-customer note; Jenna to review and sign-off. Due 2027-09-15 EOD.

Action items (consolidated)
- Sofia Chen: rollback LRU heuristic in hosted & shared dedicated pools; coordinate with release-engineering and infra. Due 2027-09-15 03:00 PT.
- Liam O'Connor: execute temporary +15% capacity bump for affected dedicated pools; confirm cost and schedule with finance. Due 2027-09-15 05:00 PT.
- Priya Menon: allocate tracing quota and coordinate KV instrumentation rollout plan. Due 2027-09-16.
- Priya Menon & Evan Brooks: produce config-diff and on-prem mitigation notes. Due 2027-09-17.
- Marco Ruiz: draft customer incident summary and mitigation steps; hand to Jenna for review. Due 2027-09-15 EOD.
- Sofia Chen & Rahul Das: run 48h test in private pool with enhanced traces, collect traces, file follow-up perf ticket. Due 2027-09-18.
- Aisha Patel (follow-up): review after rollback and convene short readout on 2027-09-16 09:00 PT to decide further permanent changes.

Risk register (short):
- Revert risk: reverting heuristics may expose a regression that had positive gains in some long-tail workloads. We maintain private test pool to capture those cases.
- Cost risk: extended capacity bump increases spend; Finance cap observed. Decision limited to 72 hours.
- Operational risk: repeated rollbacks degrade developer confidence; require stronger pre-merge perf gating.

Discussion notes / stray items recorded:
- Suggestion: add a small synthetic traffic job that mimics heavy KV reuse patterns to CI perf suite. (Liam)
- Request: product wants a short writeup on observable user-impact thresholds (when to notify accounts vs. silent mitigation). Action: Product to propose thresholds; assigned to Sofia to follow up. Due 2027-09-21.
- Quick wins: enable additional debug logs behind a flag for only affected hosts to reduce noise. (Evan)

AOB:
- On-call rotations: shift swap for SRE on 2027-09-20 — Evan to confirm.
- Next meeting: 2027-09-21 10:00 PT (standup cadence maintained).

Appendix: useful links and artifacts
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1209
- Perf trace snapshot: s3://redwood-perf/traces/2027-09-11/cache-evict-0001.json
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-4821 (cache-evict regression), JIRA-OPS-1379 (capacity bump)

End notes: this doc is a working capture of the leadership decisions and action items from the 2027-09-14 cross-team meeting. Status = draft; will update after rollback readout and once customer communications are dispatched.
